claims.text: A procedure is defined as PROCEDURE <name>(<parameters>) ... ENDPROCEDURE and called as a statement with CALL <name>(<arguments>) - it does one named job and returns no value through its name.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A procedure is appropriate where the same job is needed in several places or where it splits a long program into named steps, because the job is written once and called by name wherever it is needed.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A parameter is a variable named in a module's header through which values arrive; an argument is the value the caller passes in the call, and every parameter is already a value the module works on, so a module takes its values through its parameters rather than by INPUT inside it.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A parameter may be passed by value, where the module receives a copy and cannot change the caller's variable, or by reference, where the module works on the caller's variable itself and a change inside shows outside.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A function is defined as FUNCTION <name>(<parameters>) RETURNS <type> ... ENDFUNCTION, RETURNs a single value inside its body, and is used in an expression - its call replaced by the returned value - never after CALL.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A function is appropriate where a value must be computed and used in an expression or assigned, because the call itself carries the value back to the caller.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The module terminology: the header states the name and parameters; the interface is what the caller needs to know - the header and what the module does; the return value is what a function hands back with RETURN.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: An identifier may not be a keyword, a data type or a built-in function name such as LENGTH, CHAR or MONTH, because those names are the language's own.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Efficient pseudocode avoids repeating identical work: a job done in several places is written once as a module, a loop repeats what repeats, and a computed value is stored once rather than recomputed.
